Abstract
This paper uncovers an exact χ2 dissipation identity for the Blahut–Arimoto (BA) flow and establishes its fundamental
information-geometric structure. While prior works have analyzed BA convergence via the monotone decrease of the Kullback–
Leibler divergence, we establish that the continuous-time flow ∂τq = ˜qβ[q] −q is fundamentally governed by the Pearson χ2
divergence. Specifically, we prove the governing identity

the global non-asymptotic driver of the dynamics.
We establish a unified dissipation identity revealing that the χ2 and the symmetrised Jeffreys divergence DJ differ only by a
cubic residual N, which vanishes exactly for the BA flow. This algebraic cancellation identifies the Jacobian Kq = D˜qβ[q] and
its complement Aq = I −Kq as the Fisher–Rao Hessian of the free energy Φβ. The spectral gap of Aq∗is proved to determine
both the local exponential convergence rate (a universal value of 2 in artificial time) and the stability of the attraction basin.
For Gaussian sources, the theory yields three concrete consequences: (i) the reproduction variance obeys an exact closed ODE;
(ii) the Gaussian distribution emerges as the unique dynamical attractor; and (iii) in high dimensions, convergence is bottlenecked
by the maximum source variance—spectral stiffness. Significantly, this framework provides new dissipative interpretations for
fundamental problems including MIMO channel capacity, Wyner–Ziv coding, and the information bottleneck. These results
establish the BA flow as a canonical dissipative relaxation and provide a geometric foundation for the dynamical theory of
information-theoretic optimisation.

B. From Discrete Iterations to Continuous Dynamics
Despite the algorithm’s widespread use and well-understood convergence, a fundamental question has remained largely
unexplored:
Is there an intrinsic continuous-time dynamical system whose time-discretisation recovers the BA algorithm, and if
so, what geometric structure governs its evolution?
This question is not merely of academic interest. A continuous-time formulation exposes the infinitesimal generator of the
BA iteration: the geometric object that determines how fast the algorithm converges, what dissipation mechanisms drive it,
and how it relates to gradient flows and mirror descent in information geometry. It also opens the door to non-equilibrium
thermodynamic interpretations and to the systematic design of accelerated algorithms.
The natural continuous-time embedding of the BA iteration is the flow
∂τqτ = ˜qβ[qτ] −qτ,

whose fixed-point set coincides with the RD-optimal distributions. When the alphabets are finite, the BA operator T : ∆n →∆n
and the Jacobian Kq = DT(q) admit explicit matrix representations, providing a concrete computational handle on the abstract
geometric structures developed in this paper.
Existing geometric analyses of BA-type algorithms remain predominantly discrete, leaving the underlying infinitesimal
generator of the iteration uncharacterized. While recent Wasserstein-based approaches provide useful tools, they remain extrinsic
to the intrinsic information-theoretic structure. What is missing—and what this paper provides—is a continuous-time theory
that is (a) intrinsic to the Fisher–Rao geometry, (b) reveals the exact cubic cancellation mechanism between χ2 and Jeffreys
dissipation, and (c) yields universal, spectral-gap-determined convergence guarantees.
Throughout the paper, τ ≥0 denotes the continuous time parameter of the BA flow; all dynamics are expressed in τ alone.
Physical time interpretations (e.g., in stochastic extensions) are deferred to future work.
C. Main Contributions

predominantly analyses BA convergence through the lens of Kullback–Leibler divergence and monotone free-energy decrease,

D. Comparison with Related Work
a) Classical BA analysis.: Blahut [3] and Arimoto [4] proved convergence of the discrete iteration via monotone decrease
of the free energy, without identifying the precise dissipation measure. Csisz´ar [10], [11] characterised each BA step as an
alternating I-projection, providing a geometric picture that is fundamentally discrete. Nakagawa and Watanabe [9] derived sharp
O(1/n) convergence rates for the discrete iteration. Our continuous-time framework subsumes these results: the free-energy
decrease of Blahut–Arimoto corresponds to the exact identity ˙Φβ = −V , and the O(1/n) rate is the time-averaged counterpart
of the local exponential rate 2.
b) Information geometry and mirror descent.: Amari’s natural gradient [12] and the mirror-descent framework [13],
[14] provide the geometric language closest to our setting. Raskutti and Mukherjee [15] showed that mirror descent with KL
geometry is a natural gradient flow under the Fisher–Rao metric. We show that the BA flow is simultaneously a natural gradient
flow of Φβ (primal face) and a self-consistent mirror flow with Jeffreys dissipation (dual face), with the two perspectives unified
by the single ODE Corollary 1.
c) Bregman and EM perspectives.: Hayashi [16] reformulated discrete BA steps as Bregman EM updates, identifying a
KL proximal structure. Gilboa et al. [17] analysed the convergence of alternating Bregman projections in rate–distortion theory.
Both works treat the χ2 and KL structures as separate objects. Our unified identity Corollary 1 shows that both arise from the
same infinitesimal generator, with the cubic cancellation theorem providing the precise algebraic reason for their relationship.
d) Wasserstein gradient flows.: Wang et al. [18] proposed estimating RD functions via Wasserstein gradient descent. While
powerful, Wasserstein geometry operates via spatial mass transport and is extrinsic to the information-theoretic structure. The
BA flow, by contrast, operates via density reweighting in the Fisher–Rao weighted Hilbert space Hq, which is the natural
metric space for χ2 and KL divergences.
e) Thermodynamic analogies.: Merhav [19] and Parrondo et al. [20] have explored connections between information
theory and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. The dissipation hierarchy of Section III—χ2 as the full nonlinear drift and DJ
as the symmetric quadratic reduction—has a natural thermodynamic reading: V is analogous to total entropy production, while
DJ is analogous to the symmetrised (housekeeping + excess) decomposition familiar from stochastic thermodynamics [21].
f) Recent continuous-time formulations.: Two recent works share our motivation of endowing BA-type algorithms with
a continuous-time interpretation. He, Saunderson, and Fawzi [22] reformulated the discrete BA step as a Bregman proximal
point algorithm, revealing a KL geometry of the individual iterations. Beretta and Pelillo [23] proposed a vector flow that
computes the capacity of discrete memoryless channels and established qualitative exponential convergence via a replicator
structure. Our framework complements these contributions by providing:
(i) Continuous-time operator structure. While [22] provides a Bregman characterisation of the discrete iterations, our
continuous-time flow ∂τq = T(q) −q and its Jacobian Kq offer an infinitesimal perspective that is not directly accessible
from the discrete proximal point formulation.
(ii) Spectral rate quantification. Beretta and Pelillo [23] establish qualitative exponential convergence for DMC capacity
flows; our Hessian operator Aq = I −Kq and its spectral gap provide a quantitative rate that explicitly depends on
problem parameters.
(iii) Unified divergence dynamics. Prior works analyse χ2 or KL divergences individually. We show that both obey a single
unified dissipation identity and that the Jeffreys divergence enjoys an exact cubic cancellation, thereby linking the two
divergence geometries.

C. Foundations for a Continuous-Time Theory of Information Flows
The results of this paper transcend the specific setting of rate–distortion theory. What began as the computational recipe of
Blahut and Arimoto in 1972 is revealed here as a canonical dissipative relaxation on the statistical manifold, governed by a
single geometric principle that manifests equally as χ2 decay, Jeffreys symmetrisation, and free-energy descent.
The unified dissipation identity (59), together with the identification of the information-theoretic Hessian Aq = I −Kq as
the Fisher–Rao Hessian of the marginal free energy, provides a common language for analysing a broad class of self-consistent
algorithms that share the Gibbs-map template. Every such system can now be studied through its Jacobian Kq, its cubic residual
N, and its spectral gap Gap(Aq∗).
This perspective places the BA flow at the intersection of three active research frontiers:
• Information geometry: The correspondence between χ2 and Jeffreys dissipation, and the Bregman origin of the cubic
cancellation, suggest that the BA flow is a natural laboratory for exploring the interplay between f-divergence geometry
and dynamical stability.
• Non-equilibrium thermodynamics: The dissipation hierarchy—χ2 as total entropy production, DJ as the symmetric
(housekeeping + excess) decomposition— offers a precise information-theoretic analogue of the fluctuation relations
familiar from stochastic thermodynamics [21].
• Machine learning and neural representations: The emergence of Gaussianity as a dynamical attractor (Theorem 12)
and the spectral stiffness analysis of Section V-D provide testable predictions for the training dynamics of variational
autoencoders, diffusion models, and information-bottleneck networks.
In this sense, the present work does not merely close a five-decade gap in the understanding of the Blahut–Arimoto algorithm;
it opens a new chapter in the dynamical theory of information processing, where the evolution of beliefs, representations, and
codes is governed by the spectral geometry of the underlying statistical manifold.
D. Closing Perspective
The Blahut–Arimoto algorithm was conceived as a computational tool. The continuous-time theory developed here reveals
it as something deeper: a canonical dissipative relaxation on the statistical manifold, governed by a single geometric principle
that manifests equally as χ2 decay, Jeffreys symmetrisation, and free-energy descent.
The cubic cancellation theorem (Theorem 5) shows that the Jeffreys divergence is not merely a convenient symmetric
measure, but the natural second-order object associated with the BA flow: it is what remains when the full nonlinear dynamics
is projected onto its symmetric quadratic core. In this sense, χ2 and DJ stand in the same relation to the BA flow as kinetic
energy and free energy stand to a physical relaxation process—complementary windows onto the same underlying dynamics,
each revealing aspects the other cannot.
The universality across rate–distortion, channel capacity, information bottleneck, and Wyner–Ziv coding suggests that
this geometric duality is a fundamental organizing principle for all self-consistent information-theoretic flows, and that the
continuous-time perspective will continue to yield structural insights as the framework is extended to distributed, stochastic,
and nonconvex settings.

Abstract: This paper uncovers an exact χ2 dissipation identity for the Blahut–Arimoto (BA) flow and establishes its fundamental information-geometric structure. While prior works have analyzed BA convergence via the monotone decrease of the Kullback– Leibler divergence, we establish that the continuous-time flow ∂τq = ˜qβ[q] −q is fundamentally governed by the Pearson χ2 divergence. Specifically, we prove the governing identity d dτ Φβ = −χ2(˜qβ∥q), elevating χ2 from a mere local approximation to the global non-asymptotic driver of the dynamics. We establish a unified dissipation identity revealing that the χ2 and the symmetrised Jeffreys divergence DJ differ only by a cubic residual N, which vanishes exactly for the BA flow. This algebraic cancellation identifies the Jacobian Kq = D˜qβ[q] and its complement Aq = I −Kq as the Fisher–Rao Hessian of the free energy Φβ. The spectral gap of Aq∗is proved to determine both the local exponential convergence rate (a universal value of 2 in artificial time) and the stability of the attraction basin. For Gaussian sources, the theory yields three concrete consequences: (i) the reproduction variance obeys an exact closed ODE; (ii) the Gaussian distribution emerges as the unique dynamical attractor; and (iii) in high dimensions, convergence is bottlenecked by the maximum source variance—spectral stiffness. Significantly, this framework provides new dissipative interpretations for fundamental problems including MIMO channel capacity, Wyner–Ziv coding, and the information bottleneck. These results establish the BA flow as a canonical dissipative relaxation and provide a geometric foundation for the dynamical theory of information-theoretic optimisation.
